1.explanation: The functions itemRangeText, itemText, and pageRangeText (defined on defaultProps in both the classic and experimental Pagination) produce the footer copy. They always append the plural form (“items” or “pages”) regardless of count. To fix the bug, these functions must inspect their counts and return singular (“item” or “page”) when the total (or computed range) equals one.
1.bug_scenario: In the Pagination component (both classic and experimental implementations), when there is exactly one item or one page, the footer text still uses the plural form (“items” and “pages”). For example, with totalItems = 1 it renders “1–1 of 1 items”, and with totalPages = 1 it renders “of 1 pages”. The expected behavior is to switch to the singular form (“item” and “page”) when the count equals one.

2.explanation: The Pagination class (and its experimental variant) is responsible for rendering the footer text that shows how many items and pages exist. The defaultProps.itemRangeText, itemText, and pageRangeText functions generate the pluralized strings (“items” and “pages”) without checking for a singular case. To fix the bug, these functions (or the render logic that invokes them) need conditional logic to return “item” when totalItems === 1 and “page” when totalPages === 1, ensuring the correct singular noun is used.
2.bug_scenario: When there is only one page or one item in the Pagination component, the footer text still uses the plural form “items” or “pages”. For example, with totalItems=1 and pageSize=1 you see “1–1 of 1 items” and “of 1 pages” instead of the singular “item” and “page”.
